analyze_timeline_audio_tool.description: Report the audio role, level and speech windows of every timeline clip. Roles: speech (has transcript cues), music/sfx (audio-only, no cues), ambient (video, no cues), unknown (not indexed yet). Read this before mixing so you know which clips are beds and which carry the voice. detail='windows' also lists detected speech ranges in timeline seconds, plus warnings for overlapping voices and beds stacked above speech.

set_clip_volume_tool.description: Set one timeline clip's audio level, over the whole clip or one time window. Give exactly one of level_db (decibels, negative is quieter) or level (0.0-1.3 linear). mode='replace' sets the level outright, mode='scale' multiplies the clip's existing automation. start_seconds/end_seconds are TIMELINE seconds; omit both for a flat level over the whole clip. Use this for a static balance pass; use duck_under_speech_tool to keep music out of the way of dialogue.

duck_under_speech_tool.description: Duck music/SFX beds under speech with volume keyframes, restoring them in the gaps. Writes timeline volume automation only — no media is re-encoded and no clip changes track, position or trim. With speech_clip_ids='auto' the speech clips come from indexed transcript cues; beds default to every music/sfx clip overlapping speech. This is the correct fix when music buries the voice — never restack tracks to solve a mix problem. Use dry_run='true' to preview the envelope first.

add_clip_to_timeline_tool.description:
Place a project file on the timeline, optionally trimmed to a window.

    Trim with start_seconds + either duration_seconds or end_seconds (the keep-window
    form from search_clips_tool). Seconds only — never frames.
    Cut points are automatically pulled off mid-sentence and mid-musical-phrase using
    the file's transcript cues and chapters, so trims do not land inside dialogue.
    An optional query names the action; a wide window is vision-checked before trimming
    (a window already narrow enough is trusted as-is). Audio needs position_seconds and
    duration_seconds, or full_file="true" for one continuous bed.
    Empty track uses the bottom underlay layer.

place_motion_graphic_tool.description:
Place a HyperFrames motion graphic with overlay/gap/cut_in enforcement.

    mode=overlay: transparent files only, HIGH overlay track (never opaque over hero).
    mode=gap: opaque plate only when primary track is clear at [t, t+dur).
    mode=cut_in: opaque plate — ripple primary-track clips at/after t, then insert as a cut.
    Pass layout_region from propose_overlay_windows_tool (lower_third|corner_br|corner_tr|full_frame|mid_plate).
    Prefer this over add_clip_to_timeline_tool for MG renders.
    Watch of the key on-screen graphic is built in — watch_clip_window_tool is not needed.

delete_from_timeline_tool.description:
Delete from the timeline: one clip placement, or an entire track.

    This is the ONLY delete tool. Target it one of three ways:
      timeline_clip_id - an id from list_clips_tool or the timeline snapshot
      clip_query       - a description, narrowed with track / occurrence
                         (1-based) / position_near (timeline seconds)
      track            - clear that whole track (UI "Track 1".."N", bottom=1,
                         or a storage layer_number)

    Leave scope="auto": a clip id or query deletes ONE placement, a bare track
    clears the track. Force it with scope="clip" or scope="track".
    include_transitions also removes transitions on the track (track scope).

    Deleting leaves a gap - it never ripples. The whole call is a single undo
    step, whether it removes one clip or fifty.

search_clips_tool.description:
Search ALL indexed media in THIS project's index (videos, images, audio — deeper than tags).

    look_for: "on_screen" when the user describes who/what is VISIBLE ("the guy with the iPad"),
    "spoken" when they describe what is SAID ("when he talks about smartphones"), empty for both.
    Set it whenever the request is clearly one or the other: short visual descriptions otherwise
    match transcript lines that merely share a word.

    Returns media_bin_file_id plus start_seconds/end_seconds/peak_seconds (raw, 3dp) and M:SS for humans.
    Pass the raw *_seconds values straight to place_moment — do not convert to frames. To PLACE the moment,
    call place_moment(file_id, start_seconds, end_seconds, query) — it watches, trims, and places.
    Do not convert to frames. For moments inside one known
    timeline clip use search_clip_scenes_tool then slice_moment.

watch_clip_window_tool.description:
Vision-check whether a query is actually visible in a window of a placed clip.

    start/end are SOURCE seconds (the source media time search results report), and every
    time it returns is source seconds too. Returns the frames watched, the shot cuts in the
    window, and where the query is visible. Read-only — never edits the timeline.
    Put times ONLY in start/end, never in query. For "where does the shot change", read the
    shot cuts line instead of re-watching. To cut at a time you found, call slice_moment with
    start_seconds (and end_seconds for a range).
    place_moment / slice_moment / stock_video already watch on their own, so call this
    ONLY to check one uncertain window, then act on the answer. After a few watches with no
    edit, further watches are refused.

Propose safe timeline windows for motion-graphics (timing + layout region).

    Returns JSON windows with t / score / avoid / prefer / scene_label / track_hint /
    suggest_transparent / layout_region / place_mode (overlay|gap).
    Score uses scene regex + embedding similarity when the project index is available.
    Bake layout_region into session/draft.html; pass place_mode into place_motion_graphic_tool.
    Does NOT invent titles or block_query.
